Only `finding.text` and `chunk.content` are embedded; option codes and sales numbers stay exact, un-embedded data. Changing the model means re-embedding and altering the column — see [decision 0004](../decisions/0004-supabase-and-openai-embeddings.md) | | API | FastAPI | — | | Frontend | React + shadcn/ui | Chat thread with step cards (Accept / Edit / Retry / Reject) and a plan strip, evidence panel with citations, score breakdown, audit timeline | | Deploy | Docker-compose / Vercel demo instance; Supabase hosts the database and raw-file storage | Single environment for the demo | # Orchestration & human-in-the-loop: a chat that plans, then runs one agent at a time > Status: `draft` · Last updated: 2026-10-10 (chat entry point, orchestrator-planned agents, auto-start after accept — see [decision 0005](../decisions/0005-chat-entry-and-orchestrator-planned-steps.md)) This is the central mechanic of the whole system. The PM starts a **chat** with a research request. An **orchestrator** decides which agents are needed. They run **one at a time**, and each agent's answer is shown in the chat for the PM to push back on or accept **before the next agent starts**. Nothing is shown as a final result until every needed agent has been accepted. Earlier drafts gated the PM at the end only, then at every step but with a manual "Run" click per agent. The chat model keeps the per-step gate and removes the extra click: **accepting a step is what starts the next one.** ## Entry point: a chat 1. PM opens a **new chat** and types a research request, e.g. *"What would we need to stay competitive on seat comfort in the US market?"* Scope (vehicle line, market) is taken from the message or asked back in one short question if missing. 2. The **Orchestrator** reads the request and produces a **plan**: the ordered list of agents needed and why each is included (e.g. Customer Feedback → Competitor → Clustering → Requirements Drafting; Baseline and Market/Trend left out, with the reason). The plan is shown in the chat. The PM can edit it (add, remove, reorder) before the first agent starts. 3. The first agent starts. When it finishes, its answer appears as a step card in the chat. 4. The PM pushes back or accepts. On **Accept**, the orchestrator starts the next needed agent automatically, with the accepted output as context. The orchestrator may also revise the remaining plan based on what was found (e.g. add the Sales agent because a cluster needs an uptake cross-check); any change to the plan is announced in the chat. 5. After the last agent is accepted, the **final research result** is compiled and shown with citations. It is not shown earlier. Not every request needs every agent. A question that only needs feedback evidence runs two or three agents; a full requirement derivation runs the whole chain. ## The unit of work: a Step A `PipelineRun` (one chat request's execution, scoped to a vehicle line + market) is made of `Step`s, one per agent invocation. A step has five states: ```mermaid stateDiagram-v2 [*] --> planned: orchestrator adds it to the plan planned --> running: previous step accepted
(or first in plan), auto-start running --> awaiting_review: agent finishes,
Critic Agent has verified citations,
human-readable summary attached awaiting_review --> accepted: PM Accept awaiting_review --> running: PM Retry (steering note in chat) awaiting_review --> rejected: PM Reject accepted --> [*]: starts the next needed step rejected --> [*]: PM decides skip-this-agent or abort run ``` Deliberate points: - **Accept is the only trigger for the next agent.** No agent runs ahead of an unreviewed one, and there is no separate "Run" click. The gate is the review, not the launch. - **The Critic Agent sits inside `running → awaiting_review`**, not after it. A step doesn't reach the PM until every claim in its output has a live citation — see [`01-agents.md`](01-agents.md#the-critic-agent). The PM pushes back on judgment calls, not on obviously unsourced claims; those never arrive. - **The plan can change mid-run** (orchestrator proposes, PM can veto), but a step already `accepted` is never silently re-run. ## The four actions, same verbs as everywhere else | Action | What it does | |---|---| | **Accept** | Step → `accepted`. Its `Finding`/`Cluster`/`Requirement`/`Score` output becomes real input for the next step, and the orchestrator starts that step. | | **Edit** | PM directly rewrites the human-readable summary or the underlying structured output (e.g. merges two clusters, tightens a metric) before accepting. The diff is the audit event. | | **Retry** (= Challenge, at step grain) | PM replies in the chat with a steering note ("exclude paywalled sources," "only EU respondents," "re-check that number"). Same agent, same step, re-runs with the note appended to its task. Step goes back to `running`. | | **Reject** | Step → `rejected`. PM then decides: proceed without this agent's contribution (flagged as a coverage gap on everything downstream) or abort the run. | Pushing back is a normal chat message on the step's thread, so the conversation reads as a dialogue with the system rather than a form. This reuses the exact same four verbs as the coarser requirement lifecycle ([`05-requirement-lifecycle.md`](05-requirement-lifecycle.md)) — approve/reject/edit/challenge — just applied at the grain of one agent's output instead of one finished requirement. ## Human-readable output, every time Every agent emits two things, not one: structured output for the data model, and a short `StepSummary` — plain language, always including: - what it looked at (scope, sources, filters applied) - what it found, as a short bulleted list, **each bullet carrying its citation** (source + locator: file and page/sheet/row, or URL and retrieval date) - how confident it is, and what's thin or missing - anything it flagged as out of scope (regulatory/pricing) and routed to the side bin This is what renders in the chat as the step card. The final research result is compiled from the accepted `StepSummary`s; every statement in it can only cite findings that were retrieved and accepted along the way. ## The chain (what the orchestrator chooses from) ```mermaid flowchart TD Q["PM chat request"] --> ORCH{"Orchestrator
plans needed agents"} ORCH --> A1[Baseline Agent] ORCH --> A2[Customer Feedback Agent] ORCH --> A3[Sales & Portfolio Agent] ORCH --> A4[Competitor Agent] ORCH --> A5[Market & Trend Agent] A1 & A2 & A3 & A4 & A5 -.->|only those in the plan,
one at a time, each accepted
before the next starts| SC[Clustering / Structure & context] SC --> RD[Requirements Drafting] RD --> PR[Prioritization / Scoring] PR --> DOC[Documentation — dossier,
audit events, re-embed] DOC --> FV["Final research result
(+ requirements → Draft in the normal lifecycle)"] ``` Which of these appear in a given run is the orchestrator's decision. A pure market-research question may stop after the research agents and Clustering; Drafting, Prioritization, and Documentation are added only when the request asks for requirements. When requirements are produced, each enters the normal [lifecycle](05-requirement-lifecycle.md) at `Draft` and can still be approved, edited, rejected, or challenged individually. ## Worked example — "what features would we need to stay competitive in the US market?" 1. PM starts a new chat with that question. Orchestrator replies with a plan: *Competitor → Customer Feedback (US) → Market & Trend → Clustering → Requirements Drafting → Prioritization. Skipping Baseline (no previous-generation angle asked for).* PM adds Sales & Portfolio before Clustering and confirms. 2. Competitor Agent starts. Card: *"Searched 14 competitor review/spec sources for US midsize sedans. 6 findings: 3 competitor_advantage, 2 market_trend, 1 unmet_need. 2 sources are paywalled — flagged Interpreted."* Each finding has its URL and retrieval date. 3. PM replies **Retry**: *"drop the paywalled ones, find a free equivalent or mark unverified."* Same agent re-runs. PM reviews again and clicks **Accept**. 4. Customer Feedback Agent starts automatically (US-filtered). PM accepts. Market & Trend starts, then Sales & Portfolio — each one only after the previous was accepted. 5. Clustering starts. PM **Edits** one cluster (two themes were really the same complaint), then **Accepts**. 6. Requirements Drafting starts, then Prioritization. PM reviews the score breakdown, nudges the `business_signal` weight, re-runs, **Accepts**. 7. Last agent accepted: the final research result appears in the chat, with a citation on every claim, and the draft requirements sit in the backlog at `Draft`. Every launch, retry, edit, and accept is in the audit trail (see [`07-audit-trail.md`](07-audit-trail.md)). ## Data model additions `PipelineRun` and `Step` (full schema in [`04-data-model.md`](04-data-model.md#pipelinerun--step)), plus `Conversation` and `Message` for the chat thread: a run belongs to one conversation, step cards and PM replies are messages linked to their step. ## UI shape A chat thread. The user's request, the orchestrator's plan, each step card, and the PM's pushback replies are all messages in order. A step card in `awaiting_review` shows the `StepSummary` with citations plus **Accept / Edit / Retry / Reject**; anything else is read-only history. A plan strip at the top shows which steps are planned, running, or done. It's closer to a CI pipeline with manual approval gates, driven through a chat, than to a chatbot that answers in one go — the PM is operating the system, not just chatting with it. # Decision log Dated, append-only. Add a new numbered file rather than editing an old one when a decision changes — note the supersession in the new file and update the old one's status line. | # | Decision | Status | |---|---|---| | [0001](0001-two-tier-pdf-ingestion.md) | Two-tier PDF ingestion instead of naive text extraction | accepted | | [0002](0002-stepwise-agent-approval-chain.md) | Gate every agent step, not just the drafted requirement and its score | accepted | | [0003](0003-critic-agent-and-agent-split.md) | Add a Critic Agent; split Competitor from Market/Trend | accepted | | [0004](0004-supabase-and-openai-embeddings.md) | Supabase Postgres + pgvector for storage; OpenAI `text-embedding-3-small` for embeddings | accepted | | [0005](0005-chat-entry-and-orchestrator-planned-steps.md) | Chat entry point; orchestrator plans the agents; accepting a step starts the next | accepted | | [0006](0006-raw-tables-and-cited-pdf-chunks.md) | Load Excel as raw relational tables; chunk PDFs per page with real citations | accepted | | [0007](0007-option-availability-and-ontology-seed.md) | Parse equipment tables by position; seed the ontology from the feedback labels | accepted | | [0008](0008-knowledge-layer-normalization-and-retrieval.md) | Normalize all evidence to one vocabulary; one retrieval interface that returns citations | accepted | | [0009](0009-web-search-through-the-llm.md) | Web search runs through the LLM's built-in search tool for now, not a separate search API | accepted | # Requirement Evidence Engine — living architecture docs Start with the [software idea](idea.md) for the original model-specific product concept: vehicle specifications, PM priorities and successor targets, competitor comparisons by market, historical trends, weekly reports, and AI suggestions grounded in cited evidence. Technical architecture for the BMW "AI for Product Decision Making" hackathon challenge: a multi-agent system that turns customer feedback, product data, sales data and web research into cited, PM-approved customer requirements for a successor vehicle. These docs are **living** — they change as we build. When a design decision changes, edit the relevant file in place and add a dated entry to [`decisions/`](decisions/) explaining what changed and why, instead of leaving the old reasoning to rot silently in a doc that still reads as current. ## Status legend Each doc opens with a status line: - `draft` — shape is proposed, not yet validated against real data or code - `building` — actively being implemented, may lag the code slightly - `stable` — implemented and not expected to change before the demo ## Map | Doc | What it answers | |---|---| | [`idea.md`](idea.md) | The original software concept and the PM's model-specific decision loop | | [`architecture/00-overview.md`](architecture/00-overview.md) | What is this, in scope / out of scope, the five-stage pipeline at a glance | | [`architecture/01-agents.md`](architecture/01-agents.md) | Every agent: what it reads, what it produces, how autonomous it is | | [`architecture/02-orchestration-and-human-in-the-loop.md`](architecture/02-orchestration-and-human-in-the-loop.md) | **How the PM actually stays in control** — the chat → orchestrator plan → review-and-accept-each-agent model | | [`architecture/03-ingestion.md`](architecture/03-ingestion.md) | How a PDF or Excel file becomes a cited `Finding` | | [`architecture/04-data-model.md`](architecture/04-data-model.md) | Every entity and how they reference each other | | [`architecture/05-requirement-lifecycle.md`](architecture/05-requirement-lifecycle.md) | What happens to a requirement after it's accepted, over the ~2-year program | | [`architecture/06-prioritization.md`](architecture/06-prioritization.md) | The scoring formula and a worked example | | [`architecture/07-audit-trail.md`](architecture/07-audit-trail.md) | The event log schema that makes everything traceable | | [`architecture/08-scaling-and-config.md`](architecture/08-scaling-and-config.md) | Why this isn't hardcoded to one vehicle line or market | | [`architecture/09-tech-stack.md`](architecture/09-tech-stack.md) | What we're actually building it with, and why | | [`architecture/10-competitor-benchmarking.md`](architecture/10-competitor-benchmarking.md) | How one BMW becomes a comparable rival set, and how rival evidence is compared fairly | | [`architecture/11-knowledge-layer.md`](architecture/11-knowledge-layer.md) | How the evidence is normalized, stored with citations, and queried by the agents | ## Functional requirements What the system must do, as testable statements with IDs and priorities, in [`requirements/`](requirements/) — partly derived from the architecture docs above, partly new (PM overview, flexible feedback / website / social media inputs). Start at [`requirements/README.md`](requirements/README.md). ## Decision log Dated, append-only records of the choices that weren't obvious, in [`decisions/`](decisions/). Same philosophy as the product itself: a decision without a recorded reason is a decision nobody can push back on later. ## Source material - Official brief: `BMW_Hackathon_Briefing_Short.pdf` (provided by BMW, kept outside this repo) - Provided data: `F70`/`G60`/`G70` feedback, option lists, customer studies, `sales_volumes.xlsx` (presumed mapping: F70 → 1 Series successor, G60 → 5 Series, G70 → 7 Series — **confirm against BMW's codebook before stating this as fact**) - A rendered, presentation-friendly version of the pipeline/data-model/lifecycle diagrams in this doc set exists as a standalone artifact for pitching; these `.md` files are the source of truth for building. # attention_is_all_we_have BMW "AI for Product Decision Making" hackathon — a multi-agent system that turns customer feedback, product data, sales data, and web research into cited, PM-approved vehicle requirements. Software idea: [`docs/idea.md`](docs/idea.md). Architecture docs: [`docs/README.md`](docs/README.md). Agent/push rules: [`AGENTS.md`](AGENTS.md). ## Setup - Put the provided BMW files in `data/` (gitignored). - `.env` (gitignored): `OPENAI_API_KEY`, `SUPABASE_DB_URL` (direct connection string). - `pip install -r ingest/requirements.txt`; PDFs also need `pdftotext`/`pdfinfo` (poppler). - Schema: `supabase/migrations/` (applied to the Supabase project). ## Load and query ``` python ingest/load_pdfs.py # chunk + embed the catalog PDFs python ingest/load_excel.py # feedback, sales, customer studies python ingest/load_options.py # equipment options with per-variant availability python ingest/seed_ontology.py # domains, vehicle lines, markets, category labels python -m knowledge.tools # demo of the agent retrieval tools (search, lookups, counts, cite) python ingest/ask_pdf.py "Welche Felgen gibt es für den 5er?" --line G60 ``` ## Market & Trend Agent The first agent implementation is the Market & Trend Agent. It turns cited web research into `market_trend` findings, keeps URL + retrieval date locators, stores web source trust tiers, and leaves the step in `awaiting_review` for PM acceptance. ``` python agents/market_trend_agent.py "What comfort trends matter for premium sedans?" --vehicle-line G60 --market US --dry-run python agents/market_trend_agent.py "What comfort trends matter for premium sedans?" --vehicle-line G60 --market US --run-id ``` For deterministic demos or tests, pass `--seed-sources path/to/sources.json` with a JSON list of `url`, `title`, and `snippet` entries. To avoid OpenAI as well, pass a model-output fixture via `--draft-json`: ``` python agents/market_trend_agent.py "comfort trends" --vehicle-line G60 --market US \ --seed-sources tests/fixtures/market_trend_sources.json \ --draft-json tests/fixtures/market_trend_draft.json \ --dry-run ``` Run the local tests without external services: ``` python3 -m unittest discover -s tests ```

before the next starts| SC[Clustering / Structure & context] SC --> RD[Requirements Drafting] RD --> PR[Prioritization / Scoring] PR --> DOC[Documentation — dossier,
audit events, re-embed] DOC --> FV["Final research result
(+ requirements → Draft in the normal lifecycle)"] ``` Which of these appear in a given run is the orchestrator's decision. A pure market-research question may stop after the research agents and Clustering; Drafting, Prioritization, and Documentation are added only when the request asks for requirements. When requirements are produced, each enters the normal [lifecycle](05-requirement-lifecycle.md) at `Draft` and can still be approved, edited, rejected, or challenged individually. ## Worked example — "what features would we need to stay competitive in the US market?" 1. PM starts a new chat with that question. Orchestrator replies with a plan: *Competitor → Customer Feedback (US) → Market & Trend → Clustering → Requirements Drafting → Prioritization. Skipping Baseline (no previous-generation angle asked for).* PM adds Sales & Portfolio before Clustering and confirms. 2. Competitor Agent starts. Card: *"Searched 14 competitor review/spec sources for US midsize sedans. 6 findings: 3 competitor_advantage, 2 market_trend, 1 unmet_need. 2 sources are paywalled — flagged Interpreted."* Each finding has its URL and retrieval date. 3. PM replies **Retry**: *"drop the paywalled ones, find a free equivalent or mark unverified."* Same agent re-runs. PM reviews again and clicks **Accept**. 4. Customer Feedback Agent starts automatically (US-filtered). PM accepts. Market & Trend starts, then Sales & Portfolio — each one only after the previous was accepted. 5. Clustering starts. PM **Edits** one cluster (two themes were really the same complaint), then **Accepts**. 6. Requirements Drafting starts, then Prioritization. PM reviews the score breakdown, nudges the `business_signal` weight, re-runs, **Accepts**. 7. Last agent accepted: the final research result appears in the chat, with a citation on every claim, and the draft requirements sit in the backlog at `Draft`. Every launch, retry, edit, and accept is in the audit trail (see [`07-audit-trail.md`](07-audit-trail.md)). ## Data model additions `PipelineRun` and `Step` (full schema in [`04-data-model.md`](04-data-model.md#pipelinerun--step)), plus `Conversation` and `Message` for the chat thread: a run belongs to one conversation, step cards and PM replies are messages linked to their step. ## UI shape A chat thread. The user's request, the orchestrator's plan, each step card, and the PM's pushback replies are all messages in order. A step card in `awaiting_review` shows the `StepSummary` with citations plus **Accept / Edit / Retry / Reject**; anything else is read-only history. A plan strip at the top shows which steps are planned, running, or done. It's closer to a CI pipeline with manual approval gates, driven through a chat, than to a chatbot that answers in one go — the PM is operating the system, not just chatting with it. # Decision log Dated, append-only. Add a new numbered file rather than editing an old one when a decision changes — note the supersession in the new file and update the old one's status line. | # | Decision | Status | |---|---|---| | [0001](0001-two-tier-pdf-ingestion.md) | Two-tier PDF ingestion instead of naive text extraction | accepted | | [0002](0002-stepwise-agent-approval-chain.md) | Gate every agent step, not just the drafted requirement and its score | accepted | | [0003](0003-critic-agent-and-agent-split.md) | Add a Critic Agent; split Competitor from Market/Trend | accepted | | [0004](0004-supabase-and-openai-embeddings.md) | Supabase Postgres + pgvector for storage; OpenAI `text-embedding-3-small` for embeddings | accepted | | [0005](0005-chat-entry-and-orchestrator-planned-steps.md) | Chat entry point; orchestrator plans the agents; accepting a step starts the next | accepted | | [0006](0006-raw-tables-and-cited-pdf-chunks.md) | Load Excel as raw relational tables; chunk PDFs per page with real citations | accepted | | [0007](0007-option-availability-and-ontology-seed.md) | Parse equipment tables by position; seed the ontology from the feedback labels | accepted | | [0008](0008-knowledge-layer-normalization-and-retrieval.md) | Normalize all evidence to one vocabulary; one retrieval interface that returns citations | accepted | | [0009](0009-web-search-through-the-llm.md) | Web search runs through the LLM's built-in search tool for now, not a separate search API | accepted | # Requirement Evidence Engine — living architecture docs Start with the [software idea](idea.md) for the original model-specific product concept: vehicle specifications, PM priorities and successor targets, competitor comparisons by market, historical trends, weekly reports, and AI suggestions grounded in cited evidence. Technical architecture for the BMW "AI for Product Decision Making" hackathon challenge: a multi-agent system that turns customer feedback, product data, sales data and web research into cited, PM-approved customer requirements for a successor vehicle. These docs are **living** — they change as we build. When a design decision changes, edit the relevant file in place and add a dated entry to [`decisions/`](decisions/) explaining what changed and why, instead of leaving the old reasoning to rot silently in a doc that still reads as current. ## Status legend Each doc opens with a status line: - `draft` — shape is proposed, not yet validated against real data or code - `building` — actively being implemented, may lag the code slightly - `stable` — implemented and not expected to change before the demo ## Map | Doc | What it answers | |---|---| | [`idea.md`](idea.md) | The original software concept and the PM's model-specific decision loop | | [`architecture/00-overview.md`](architecture/00-overview.md) | What is this, in scope / out of scope, the five-stage pipeline at a glance | | [`architecture/01-agents.md`](architecture/01-agents.md) | Every agent: what it reads, what it produces, how autonomous it is | | [`architecture/02-orchestration-and-human-in-the-loop.md`](architecture/02-orchestration-and-human-in-the-loop.md) | **How the PM actually stays in control** — the chat → orchestrator plan → review-and-accept-each-agent model | | [`architecture/03-ingestion.md`](architecture/03-ingestion.md) | How a PDF or Excel file becomes a cited `Finding` | | [`architecture/04-data-model.md`](architecture/04-data-model.md) | Every entity and how they reference each other | | [`architecture/05-requirement-lifecycle.md`](architecture/05-requirement-lifecycle.md) | What happens to a requirement after it's accepted, over the ~2-year program | | [`architecture/06-prioritization.md`](architecture/06-prioritization.md) | The scoring formula and a worked example | | [`architecture/07-audit-trail.md`](architecture/07-audit-trail.md) | The event log schema that makes everything traceable | | [`architecture/08-scaling-and-config.md`](architecture/08-scaling-and-config.md) | Why this isn't hardcoded to one vehicle line or market | | [`architecture/09-tech-stack.md`](architecture/09-tech-stack.md) | What we're actually building it with, and why | | [`architecture/10-competitor-benchmarking.md`](architecture/10-competitor-benchmarking.md) | How one BMW becomes a comparable rival set, and how rival evidence is compared fairly | | [`architecture/11-knowledge-layer.md`](architecture/11-knowledge-layer.md) | How the evidence is normalized, stored with citations, and queried by the agents | ## Functional requirements What the system must do, as testable statements with IDs and priorities, in [`requirements/`](requirements/) — partly derived from the architecture docs above, partly new (PM overview, flexible feedback / website / social media inputs). Start at [`requirements/README.md`](requirements/README.md). ## Decision log Dated, append-only records of the choices that weren't obvious, in [`decisions/`](decisions/). Same philosophy as the product itself: a decision without a recorded reason is a decision nobody can push back on later. ## Source material - Official brief: `BMW_Hackathon_Briefing_Short.pdf` (provided by BMW, kept outside this repo) - Provided data: `F70`/`G60`/`G70` feedback, option lists, customer studies, `sales_volumes.xlsx` (presumed mapping: F70 → 1 Series successor, G60 → 5 Series, G70 → 7 Series — **confirm against BMW's codebook before stating this as fact**) - A rendered, presentation-friendly version of the pipeline/data-model/lifecycle diagrams in this doc set exists as a standalone artifact for pitching; these `.md` files are the source of truth for building. # attention_is_all_we_have BMW "AI for Product Decision Making" hackathon — a multi-agent system that turns customer feedback, product data, sales data, and web research into cited, PM-approved vehicle requirements. Software idea: [`docs/idea.md`](docs/idea.md). Architecture docs: [`docs/README.md`](docs/README.md). Agent/push rules: [`AGENTS.md`](AGENTS.md). ## Setup - Put the provided BMW files in `data/` (gitignored). - `.env` (gitignored): `OPENAI_API_KEY`, `SUPABASE_DB_URL` (direct connection string). - `pip install -r ingest/requirements.txt`; PDFs also need `pdftotext`/`pdfinfo` (poppler). - Schema: `supabase/migrations/` (applied to the Supabase project). ## Load and query ``` python ingest/load_pdfs.py # chunk + embed the catalog PDFs python ingest/load_excel.py # feedback, sales, customer studies python ingest/load_options.py # equipment options with per-variant availability python ingest/seed_ontology.py # domains, vehicle lines, markets, category labels python -m knowledge.tools # demo of the agent retrieval tools (search, lookups, counts, cite) python ingest/ask_pdf.py "Welche Felgen gibt es für den 5er?" --line G60 ``` ## Market & Trend Agent The first agent implementation is the Market & Trend Agent. It turns cited web research into `market_trend` findings, keeps URL + retrieval date locators, stores web source trust tiers, and leaves the step in `awaiting_review` for PM acceptance. ``` python agents/market_trend_agent.py "What comfort trends matter for premium sedans?" --vehicle-line G60 --market US --dry-run python agents/market_trend_agent.py "What comfort trends matter for premium sedans?" --vehicle-line G60 --market US --run-id ``` For deterministic demos or tests, pass `--seed-sources path/to/sources.json` with a JSON list of `url`, `title`, and `snippet` entries. To avoid OpenAI as well, pass a model-output fixture via `--draft-json`: ``` python agents/market_trend_agent.py "comfort trends" --vehicle-line G60 --market US \ --seed-sources tests/fixtures/market_trend_sources.json \ --draft-json tests/fixtures/market_trend_draft.json \ --dry-run ``` Run the local tests without external services: ``` python3 -m unittest discover -s tests ``` "}

+# Product Intelligence frontend
+
+A working, responsive PM workspace based on [`docs/idea.md`](../docs/idea.md),
+[`design.md`](../design.md), and the architecture docs. Uses the documented BMW blue,
+white, and navy palette, rectangular controls, Inter, and Phosphor icons.
+
+## Run locally
+
+Use Node 24 LTS (or another version supported by Vite 7).
+
+```bash
+cd frontend
+npm ci
+npm run dev
+```
+
+Open the local URL printed by Vite. Production build:
+
+```bash
+npm run build
+npm run preview
+```
+
+## What works
+
+- Overview with vehicle-line/market selection, baseline comparisons, editable successor
+  targets and priorities, illustrative trend charts, and decision history.
+- Requirement portfolio with search, filters, explainable weighted scores, editing,
+  reason-required approval/challenge/rejection, and filtered CSV exports with citations.
+- Guided research with sequential Accept/Edit/Retry/Reject gates. Rejections require a
+  continue-with-gap or abort decision. Drafts appear only after the final review.
+- Evidence library with source locators, linked requirements, coverage gaps, and local
+  document registration. Text/CSV/JSON files include a preview; binary files are not parsed.
+- Programme report with targets, requirements, citations, history, CSV export, and
+  browser print/save as PDF.
+- Browser persistence, JSON workspace export, and an explicit reset confirmation.
+
+All seed values, excerpts, grades, and trends are **illustrative demo fixtures**, not verified
+BMW specifications or findings. Research does not call an AI provider, query Supabase, or
+search the web. Retry records steering against the same fixtures. Plans use three fixed
+steps, rather than the proposed live orchestrator. No automated report scheduling runs.
+
+Edits and previews are stored in this browser's local storage. There is no account system,
+server persistence, shared workspace, immutable audit log, or restore-from-JSON UI yet.
+Export a backup to retain work outside this browser. See
+[decision 0010](../docs/decisions/0010-local-demo-frontend-and-vercel.md) for the boundary
+between the delivered frontend and the planned backend.
+
+## Verification
+
+```bash
+npx playwright install chromium
+npm test
+```
+
+Playwright exercises desktop and mobile workflows, persistence, exports, review gates,
+keyboard dialog focus, PDF generation, overflow, and automated axe WCAG checks on all five
+views. Tests require a browser environment that permits Chromium to launch.
+
+## Structure
+
+- `src/App.tsx`: navigation, scope, dialogs, and persisted workspace state.
+- `src/data.ts`: typed demo fixtures, scoring, citations, CSV, and export utilities.
+- `src/context.tsx`: shared workspace actions.
+- `src/components/`: the five views, forms, and Radix-based dialog/button primitives.
+- `src/styles.css`: brand tokens, responsive layouts, print, and reduced-motion styles.
+
+## Vercel
+
+Deploy **this directory** as a Vite project, with `npm run build` and output directory
+`dist`. `vercel.json` contains these settings. Hash navigation allows all workspace views
+to load and refresh from the static entry point. The Latin Inter font is hosted with the
+app; the frontend needs no environment variables or backend credentials.
+
+```bash
+cd frontend
+vercel --prod
+```
+
+`.vercelignore` excludes dependencies, test artifacts, and environment files from uploads.
+Keep service-role/database/AI keys on a future backend; do not expose them through `VITE_*`.

+# 0010 — Local demo PM workspace and static Vercel deployment
+
+Date: 2026-10-10 · Status: **accepted**
+
+## Context
+
+The software idea describes a vehicle-specific PM overview, successor targets, evidence,
+competitor comparisons, trends, and reports. The repo now has ingestion, a knowledge layer,
+and a Market & Trend Agent prototype, but no frontend API or complete live orchestration
+service. The user requested a working frontend using the documented design and Vercel hosting.
+
+## Decision
+
+Deliver a React/TypeScript Vite workspace in `frontend/`, deployed independently as a static
+Vercel application. Use BMW tokens from `design.md`, self-hosted Inter, Phosphor icons, and
+Radix dialog/Slot primitives with variant-based buttons following the shadcn component pattern.
+No shadcn generator or Tailwind dependency is introduced.
+
+Implement five views: Overview, Requirements, Research, Evidence library, and Reports. Local
+state supports editable targets and requirement scores, PM decisions with reasons, sequential
+review gates, source locators, exports, and a decision history. Scope covers the documented
+F70/G60/G70 vehicle codes and EU/US/CN markets with explicitly illustrative fixtures.
+
+Use browser local storage for this demo; all data is clearly labeled illustrative. Research
+uses a fixed three-step fixture plan. Accept advances one step, Edit records a revised summary,
+Retry records steering without collecting new evidence, and Reject requires an explicit gap
+or abort decision. Draft creation waits for the last review. Uploaded files are registered
+locally; binary parsing is pending and text previews are unverified.
+
+## Consequences

# 0010 — Local demo PM workspace and static Vercel deployment

Date: 2026-10-10 · Status: **accepted**

## Context

The software idea describes a vehicle-specific PM overview, successor targets, evidence,
competitor comparisons, trends, and reports. The repo now has ingestion, a knowledge layer,
and a Market & Trend Agent prototype, but no frontend API or complete live orchestration
service. The user requested a working frontend using the documented design and Vercel hosting.

## Decision

Deliver a React/TypeScript Vite workspace in `frontend/`, deployed independently as a static
Vercel application. Use BMW tokens from `design.md`, self-hosted Inter, Phosphor icons, and
Radix dialog/Slot primitives with variant-based buttons following the shadcn component pattern.
No shadcn generator or Tailwind dependency is introduced.

Implement five views: Overview, Requirements, Research, Evidence library, and Reports. Local
state supports editable targets and requirement scores, PM decisions with reasons, sequential
review gates, source locators, exports, and a decision history. Scope covers the documented
F70/G60/G70 vehicle codes and EU/US/CN markets with explicitly illustrative fixtures.

Use browser local storage for this demo; all data is clearly labeled illustrative. Research
uses a fixed three-step fixture plan. Accept advances one step, Edit records a revised summary,
Retry records steering without collecting new evidence, and Reject requires an explicit gap
or abort decision. Draft creation waits for the last review. Uploaded files are registered
locally; binary parsing is pending and text previews are unverified.

## Consequences

- The UI can be demonstrated without database access, provider credentials, or runtime API
  dependencies. No real BMW source files, `.env`, or service keys are part of the deployment.
- Vercel hosts only the frontend. This does not deploy or replace the Python agents, ingestion,
  Supabase schema, or the proposed LangGraph/FastAPI backend.
- Client history is editable browser data, not an immutable server audit trail. There is no
  authentication, shared persistence, automatic web research, or weekly report scheduler.
- A live integration must replace fixtures with scoped, cited API responses, authenticated
  persistence, server audit events, and resumable orchestration before claiming production
  evidence handling. The backend architecture remains the target design.
- Verify the UI with a production build and desktop/mobile browser tests, including review
  gates, persistence, citations, exports, keyboard focus, and automated accessibility checks.

# Product Intelligence frontend

A working, responsive PM workspace based on [`docs/idea.md`](../docs/idea.md),
[`design.md`](../design.md), and the architecture docs. Uses the documented BMW blue,
white, and navy palette, rectangular controls, Inter, and Phosphor icons.

## Run locally

Use Node 24 LTS (or another version supported by Vite 7).

```bash
cd frontend
npm ci
npm run dev
```

Open the local URL printed by Vite. Production build:

```bash
npm run build
npm run preview
```

## What works

- Overview with vehicle-line/market selection, baseline comparisons, editable successor
  targets and priorities, illustrative trend charts, and decision history.
- Requirement portfolio with search, filters, explainable weighted scores, editing,
  reason-required approval/challenge/rejection, and filtered CSV exports with citations.
- Guided research with sequential Accept/Edit/Retry/Reject gates. Rejections require a
  continue-with-gap or abort decision. Drafts appear only after the final review.
- Evidence library with source locators, linked requirements, coverage gaps, and local
  document registration. Text/CSV/JSON files include a preview; binary files are not parsed.
- Programme report with targets, requirements, citations, history, CSV export, and
  browser print/save as PDF.
- Browser persistence, JSON workspace export, and an explicit reset confirmation.

All seed values, excerpts, grades, and trends are **illustrative demo fixtures**, not verified
BMW specifications or findings. Research does not call an AI provider, query Supabase, or
search the web. Retry records steering against the same fixtures. Plans use three fixed
steps, rather than the proposed live orchestrator. No automated report scheduling runs.

Edits and previews are stored in this browser's local storage. There is no account system,
server persistence, shared workspace, immutable audit log, or restore-from-JSON UI yet.
Export a backup to retain work outside this browser. See
[decision 0010](../docs/decisions/0010-local-demo-frontend-and-vercel.md) for the boundary
between the delivered frontend and the planned backend.

## Verification

```bash
npx playwright install chromium
npm test
```

Playwright exercises desktop and mobile workflows, persistence, exports, review gates,
keyboard dialog focus, PDF generation, overflow, and automated axe WCAG checks on all five
views. Tests require a browser environment that permits Chromium to launch.

## Structure

- `src/App.tsx`: navigation, scope, dialogs, and persisted workspace state.
- `src/data.ts`: typed demo fixtures, scoring, citations, CSV, and export utilities.
- `src/context.tsx`: shared workspace actions.
- `src/components/`: the five views, forms, and Radix-based dialog/button primitives.
- `src/styles.css`: brand tokens, responsive layouts, print, and reduced-motion styles.

## Vercel

Deploy **this directory** as a Vite project, with `npm run build` and output directory
`dist`. `vercel.json` contains these settings. Hash navigation allows all workspace views
to load and refresh from the static entry point. The Latin Inter font is hosted with the
app; the frontend needs no environment variables or backend credentials.

```bash
cd frontend
vercel --prod
```

`.vercelignore` excludes dependencies, test artifacts, and environment files from uploads.
Keep service-role/database/AI keys on a future backend; do not expose them through `VITE_*`.

# Agent rules

Project: BMW hackathon requirement-evidence engine. Architecture docs live in `docs/`
(start at `docs/README.md`); those `.md` files are the source of truth.

## UI design

- Before generating or changing UI, read `design.md` and `docs/ui-design-guidelines.md`.
- Use the BMW tokens and component rules in `design.md` for all UI.
- Apply the anti-slop workflow in `docs/ui-design-guidelines.md`. BMW's explicit brand rules
  take precedence over generic aesthetic defaults, including white surfaces, Inter fallback,
  rectangular components, and dark hero bands.

## Pushing

1. **Only push when the user asks.** Never push on your own initiative.
2. **Always squash before pushing.** Collapse all local work since the branch diverged from
   `main` into a single commit (`git reset --soft $(git merge-base HEAD origin/main)` then
   commit, or `git merge-base` + `git rebase -i` equivalent without interactive flags). One push
   = one commit.
3. **Commit message:** imperative subject line, then a short body listing what changed and why.
   Mention any `docs/decisions/` entry added or changed.
4. **Never push to `main` directly** unless the user explicitly says so; work on a branch and
   open a PR. Never force-push `main`. Force-pushing your own feature branch after a squash is
   fine (`--force-with-lease`).
5. **Never commit** `data/` (BMW-provided files), `.env`, or any secret. Check `git status`
   before committing; if any of those show up as staged, stop and fix `.gitignore`.

## Docs and design decisions

- When a design decision changes, edit the relevant `docs/architecture/*.md` in place, bump its
  `Last updated` date, and add a dated entry in `docs/decisions/` (see `docs/decisions/README.md`).
  Do this in the same commit as the code change that motivated it.

## Syncing to Supabase after a push

After a successful push, sync the project record to Supabase (use the Supabase MCP tools):

1. Upsert every new or changed `docs/decisions/*.md` entry into the `design_decisions` table
   (`id`, `title`, `status`, `body`, `source_path`, `commit_sha`, `updated_at`).
2. Upsert changed `docs/architecture/*.md` files into the `architecture_docs` table
   (`path`, `title`, `status`, `body`, `commit_sha`, `updated_at`).
3. Schema changes go through `apply_migration` (never ad-hoc DDL via `execute_sql`), and the
   migration file is committed in the same squashed commit.
4. Inspect existing tables (`list_tables`) before changing schema. Run `get_advisors` after DDL.
5. Report what was synced in the final message. If a sync step fails or is skipped, say so
   explicitly. Do not claim the sync is done.

The git repo is the source of truth; Supabase is a mirror. Never edit docs only in Supabase.

# Agent rules

Project: BMW hackathon requirement-evidence engine. Architecture docs live in `docs/`
(start at `docs/README.md`); those `.md` files are the source of truth.

## Repository layout

- `backend/` FastAPI app and Python package `app` (`api/`, `knowledge/`, `agents/`, `ingest/`,
  `orchestration/`), tests in `backend/tests/`. Run with `make backend`, test with `make test`.
- `frontend/` Vite + React + TypeScript + Tailwind + shadcn/ui. Run with `make frontend`, build with `make build`.
- `supabase/migrations/` SQL migrations, `docs/` architecture and decisions, `skills/` agent skills,
  `data/` provided BMW files (gitignored). One `.env` at the repo root. See `docs/architecture/12-repo-structure.md`.
- The frontend talks to the backend only through `/api`; it never touches the database directly.
- Put new Python code under `backend/app/`, import it as `app.<package>`, and run scripts as
  `python -m app.<package>.<module>`.

## UI design

- Before generating or changing UI, read `design.md` and `docs/ui-design-guidelines.md`.
- Use the BMW tokens and component rules in `design.md` for all UI.
- Apply the anti-slop workflow in `docs/ui-design-guidelines.md`. BMW's explicit brand rules
  take precedence over generic aesthetic defaults, including white surfaces, Inter fallback,
  rectangular components, and dark hero bands.

## Database

- Postgres on Supabase (pgvector). To connect, set up a machine or teammate, check the state, apply
  migrations, load data or fix a connection error, read `skills/database-setup/SKILL.md` first.
- Check the connection with `python skills/database-setup/scripts/check_db.py --openai`.
- Never print, log, commit or paste secrets (`SUPABASE_DB_URL`, `OPENAI_API_KEY`, passwords, keys).
- Agents read evidence through `backend/app/knowledge/tools.py`, not hand-written SQL.

## Pushing

1. **Only push when the user asks.** Never push on your own initiative.
2. **Always squash before pushing.** Collapse all local work since the branch diverged from
   `main` into a single commit (`git reset --soft $(git merge-base HEAD origin/main)` then
   commit, or `git merge-base` + `git rebase -i` equivalent without interactive flags). One push
   = one commit.
3. **Commit message:** imperative subject line, then a short body listing what changed and why.
   Mention any `docs/decisions/` entry added or changed.
4. **Never push to `main` directly** unless the user explicitly says so; work on a branch and
   open a PR. Never force-push `main`. Force-pushing your own feature branch after a squash is
   fine (`--force-with-lease`).
5. **Never commit** `data/` (BMW-provided files), `.env`, or any secret. Check `git status`
   before committing; if any of those show up as staged, stop and fix `.gitignore`.

## Docs and design decisions

- When a design decision changes, edit the relevant `docs/architecture/*.md` in place, bump its
  `Last updated` date, and add a dated entry in `docs/decisions/` (see `docs/decisions/README.md`).
  Do this in the same commit as the code change that motivated it.

## Syncing to Supabase after a push

After a successful push, sync the project record to Supabase. Any agent can do this from a shell:

1. Run `python skills/database-setup/scripts/sync_docs.py` from a checkout of the pushed commit. It
   upserts `docs/decisions/*.md` into `design_decisions` and `docs/architecture/*.md` into
   `architecture_docs` with the commit sha. (Supabase MCP tools may be used instead if available.)
2. Schema changes go through `python skills/database-setup/scripts/apply_migration.py <file>`
   (try `--dry-run` first), never ad-hoc DDL, and the migration file is committed in the same
   squashed commit.
3. Check the current state with `python skills/database-setup/scripts/check_db.py` before changing
   schema, and review the Supabase advisors after DDL.
4. Report what was synced in the final message. If a sync step fails or is skipped, say so
   explicitly. Do not claim the sync is done.

The git repo is the source of truth; Supabase is a mirror. Never edit docs only in Supabase.

Project: BMW hackathon requirement-evidence engine. Architecture docs live in `docs/`

## Repository layout

- `backend/` FastAPI app and Python package `app` (`api/`, `knowledge/`, `agents/`, `ingest/`,
  `orchestration/`), tests in `backend/tests/`. Run with `make backend`, test with `make test`.

- Put new Python code under `backend/app/`, import it as `app.<package>`, and run scripts as
  `python -m app.<package>.<module>`.

## UI design

- Before generating or changing UI, read `design.md` and `docs/ui-design-guidelines.md`.
- Use the BMW tokens and component rules in `design.md` for all UI.
- Apply the anti-slop workflow in `docs/ui-design-guidelines.md`. BMW's explicit brand rules
  take precedence over generic aesthetic defaults, including white surfaces, Inter fallback,
  rectangular components, and dark hero bands.

## Database

- Postgres on Supabase (pgvector). To connect, set up a machine or teammate, check the state, apply
  migrations, load data or fix a connection error, read `skills/database-setup/SKILL.md` first.
- Check the connection with `python skills/database-setup/scripts/check_db.py --openai`.
- Never print, log, commit or paste secrets (`SUPABASE_DB_URL`, `OPENAI_API_KEY`, passwords, keys).
- Agents read evidence through `backend/app/knowledge/tools.py`, not hand-written SQL.

## Pushing

1. **Only push when the user asks.** Never push on your own initiative.
2. **Always squash before pushing.** Collapse all local work since the branch diverged from
   `main` into a single commit (`git reset --soft $(git merge-base HEAD origin/main)` then
   commit, or `git merge-base` + `git rebase -i` equivalent without interactive flags). One push
   = one commit.
3. **Commit message:** imperative subject line, then a short body listing what changed and why.
   Mention any `docs/decisions/` entry added or changed.
4. **Never push to `main` directly** unless the user explicitly says so; work on a branch and
   open a PR. Never force-push `main`. Force-pushing your own feature branch after a squash is
   fine (`--force-with-lease`).
5. **Never commit** `data/` (BMW-provided files), `.env`, or any secret. Check `git status`
   before committing; if any of those show up as staged, stop and fix `.gitignore`.

- When a design decision changes, edit the relevant `docs/architecture/*.md` in place, bump its
  `Last updated` date, and add a dated entry in `docs/decisions/` (see `docs/decisions/README.md`).
  Do this in the same commit as the code change that motivated it.

After a successful push, sync the project record to Supabase. Any agent can do this from a shell:

1. Run `python skills/database-setup/scripts/sync_docs.py` from a checkout of the pushed commit. It
   upserts `docs/decisions/*.md` into `design_decisions` and `docs/architecture/*.md` into
   `architecture_docs` with the commit sha. (Supabase MCP tools may be used instead if available.)

3. Check the current state with `python skills/database-setup/scripts/check_db.py` before changing
   schema, and review the Supabase advisors after DDL.
4. Report what was synced in the final message. If a sync step fails or is skipped, say so
   explicitly. Do not claim the sync is done.

---
name: database-setup
description: Connect to and set up the project's Supabase Postgres database (pgvector) with an OpenAI API key. Use when a task needs database access, when a connection or OpenAI call fails, when setting up a new machine or teammate, when applying or writing migrations, or when loading the BMW data. Works from any agent shell with Python; no MCP or vendor-specific tool required.
---

# Database setup (Supabase Postgres + pgvector, OpenAI embeddings)

One Supabase project holds everything: raw evidence, embeddings, findings, requirements, audit log.
Everything below runs from a plain shell with Python, so it works the same for OpenAI Codex, ChatGPT
agents, Claude Code, Cursor or a human. Agents that have a Supabase MCP connection may use it, but
nothing here depends on it.

Never print, log, commit or paste a password, connection string or API key. Refer to variable names only.

## 1. Prerequisites

- Python 3.11+ and `make install` (or `python3 -m venv .venv && .venv/bin/pip install -e "backend[dev]"`); installs `fastapi`, `openai`, `psycopg`, `pdfplumber`, `openpyxl`, `python-dotenv`
- `pdftotext` / `pdfinfo` (poppler) only to re-run the PDF loaders
- The BMW files in `data/` (gitignored) only to re-run loaders. The data is already loaded.
- A Supabase login or database role from the project owner (section 6) and an OpenAI API key

## 2. Configure `.env` (repo root, gitignored)

```
OPENAI_API_KEY=sk-...                  # your own key
SUPABASE_DB_URL=REDACTED
OPENAI_CHAT_MODEL=gpt-4o-mini          # optional: model used by `app.ingest.ask_pdf` and `app.ingest.seed_ontology`
```

Each variable on its own line (a file without a trailing newline glues the next line on). URL-encode
special characters in the password (`@` is `%40`, `/` is `%2F`).

**OpenAI usage in this project**
- Embeddings: `text-embedding-3-small`, 1536 dimensions, fixed in the database columns. Used by the loaders
  and by every search in `backend/app/knowledge/tools.py`. The key needs embeddings access.
- Chat/answers: `OPENAI_CHAT_MODEL` (default `gpt-4o-mini`). Change it freely; it does not affect stored data.
- Switching the embedding model means re-embedding all rows and altering the vector columns.
- Costs are small: the full dataset (~14k comments, 149 PDF chunks) embeds for a few cents.

**Where the database string comes from:** Supabase dashboard -> **Connect** -> Connection string.

| Option | Host looks like | Use when |
|---|---|---|
| **Direct** | `db.<project-ref>.supabase.co:5432`, user `postgres` | your network has IPv6 |
| **Session pooler** | `aws-0-<region>.pooler.supabase.com:5432`, user `postgres.<project-ref>` | IPv4-only network; also what LangGraph's checkpointer needs |
| Transaction pooler | port `6543` | **do not use**: breaks prepared statements used by psycopg |

Teammates should use their own role (section 6), not the `postgres` admin password.

## 3. Verify

```
python skills/database-setup/scripts/check_db.py --openai   # or: make check-db
```

Checks the variables, connects, and reports pgvector, every expected table with row counts, the search
functions and the vector indexes. `--openai` also makes one tiny embeddings call to prove the key, the
model and the 1536-dimension size. Exit code 0 means ready. Expected row counts today: `feedback_raw`
13,771, `chunk` 149, `option` 198, `option_availability` 1,352, `sales_volume` 36, `study_response` 1,627;
`finding` and the tables after it are empty until agents write to them.

Then try the retrieval tools: `python -m app.knowledge.tools` (from `backend/`, or after `pip install -e backend`).

## 4. Schema and migrations

- Migrations live in `supabase/migrations/`, applied in filename order. The file in the repo must match
  what was applied.
- **Apply a migration with the script** (works from any shell, no client timeout):

```
python skills/database-setup/scripts/apply_migration.py supabase/migrations/<file>.sql --dry-run   # test, rolls back
python skills/database-setup/scripts/apply_migration.py supabase/migrations/<file>.sql             # apply for real
```

  It runs the file in one transaction, records it in `supabase_migrations.schema_migrations` (so the
  history stays complete), skips a name that is already recorded, and rolls back on any error.
  Do not apply schema changes with ad-hoc SQL. Inspect the current state first (`check_db.py`), and
  afterwards check Supabase's security and performance advisors in the dashboard.
- **Heavy migrations:** rewriting all 13.7k `feedback_raw` rows with the HNSW index takes minutes. For a bulk
  update, drop the HNSW index first, update in one pass, rebuild the index after. If another tool's
  call times out, the server may still be running the statement: look for a running `begin;` in
  `pg_stat_activity` and wait before re-submitting.
- Every table has row level security enabled and **no policies**: only the service role, the `postgres`
  admin, or a role with explicit policies can read or write. The browser/anon key sees nothing.
- `audit_event` is append-only (a trigger blocks update, delete, truncate). Never work around it.

## 5. Load the data (only on a fresh database)

Run in this order (after `pip install -e backend`, from any directory); each loader is idempotent (re-running replaces that file's rows):

```
python -m app.ingest.load_pdfs     # catalog PDFs -> source + chunk (embedded with OpenAI)
python -m app.ingest.load_options  # equipment tables -> option + option_availability
python -m app.ingest.load_excel    # feedback, sales, customer studies (feedback is embedded)
python -m app.ingest.seed_ontology # domains, vehicle lines, markets, category labels (uses the chat model)
```

Loaders connect with `autocommit=True` so each transaction block really commits. A plain connection
with a query before the block silently rolls everything back on close.

## 6. Giving a teammate access

Prefer, in this order:

1. **Dashboard access:** Organization settings -> Team -> Invite, role **Developer** (read-only for viewers).
   They sign in with their own account.
2. **A database role for scripts**, so nobody needs the `postgres` password. Template (tested; run as admin
   and replace the password with a generated one):

```sql
create role team_rw login password '<generated>';
grant usage on schema public, extensions to team_rw;
grant select, insert, update, delete on all tables in schema public to team_rw;
grant execute on all functions in schema public to team_rw;
do $$ declare t text; begin
  for t in select tablename from pg_tables where schemaname = 'public' loop

```

Each variable on its own line (a file without a trailing newline glues the next line on). URL-encode
special characters in the password (`@` is `%40`, `/` is `%2F`).

**OpenAI usage in this project**
- Embeddings: `text-embedding-3-small`, 1536 dimensions, fixed in the database columns. Used by the loaders
  and by every search in `backend/app/knowledge/tools.py`. The key needs embeddings access.

- Switching the embedding model means re-embedding all rows and altering the vector columns.

|---|---|---|
| **Direct** | `db.<project-ref>.supabase.co:5432`, user `postgres` | your network has IPv6 |
| **Session pooler** | `aws-0-<region>.pooler.supabase.com:5432`, user `postgres.<project-ref>` | IPv4-only network; also what LangGraph's checkpointer needs |
| Transaction pooler | port `6543` | **do not use**: breaks prepared statements used by psycopg |

```

"""Settings and paths shared by the API, the agents and the ingest scripts.

The repository root holds the single `.env` and the gitignored `data/` folder, so everything works
from any working directory. Secrets are read from the environment only and never logged.
"""
from __future__ import annotations

import os
from dataclasses import dataclass
from pathlib import Path

from dotenv import load_dotenv

REPO_ROOT = Path(__file__).resolve().parents[2]
DATA_DIR = REPO_ROOT / "data"
ENV_FILE = REPO_ROOT / ".env"


def load_env() -> None:
    """Load the repo-root .env (does not override variables already set in the environment)."""
    load_dotenv(ENV_FILE)


@dataclass(frozen=True)
class Settings:
    db_url: str | None
    openai_api_key_set: bool
    openai_chat_model: str
    embed_model: str
    cors_origins: list[str]


def get_settings() -> Settings:
    load_env()
    origins = os.environ.get("CORS_ORIGINS", "http://localhost:5173,http://127.0.0.1:5173")
    return Settings(
        db_url=os.environ.get("SUPABASE_DB_URL"),
        openai_api_key_set=bool(os.environ.get("OPENAI_API_KEY")),
        openai_chat_model=os.environ.get("OPENAI_CHAT_MODEL", "gpt-4o-mini"),
        embed_model="text-embedding-3-small",
        cors_origins=[o.strip() for o in origins.split(",") if o.strip()],
    )

# Repository structure: frontend and backend > Status: `building` · Last updated: 2026-10-11 (see [decision 0010](../decisions/0010-frontend-backend-repo-structure.md)) ```mermaid flowchart LR UI["frontend
React + shadcn/ui"] -->|"/api (JSON)"| API["backend
FastAPI"] API --> K["knowledge layer
retrieval tools"] API --> O["orchestration
step state machine"] O --> AG["agents"] AG --> K K --> DB[("Supabase Postgres
+ pgvector")] ING["ingest
loaders, parsers"] --> DB AG -->|findings| DB K -.->|embeddings, answers| OAI["OpenAI API"] ``` The browser never talks to the database or to OpenAI. The only door is the backend's `/api`. ## Layout ``` backend/ pyproject.toml dependencies, pytest config; `pip install -e "backend[dev]"` app/ main.py FastAPI app (CORS, routers) config.py repo-root .env and data/ paths, settings; no secrets in logs api/ HTTP layer: health, evidence search / counts / cite / filters, response schemas knowledge/ retrieval tools every agent uses; each hit carries a citation agents/ LLM-backed agents (Market & Trend today) orchestration/ step state machine (planned, running, awaiting_review, accepted, rejected) ingest/ loaders and parsers for the provided PDFs and Excel files tests/ pytest; no database or OpenAI key needed frontend/ src/ components/ui/ shadcn/ui components (generated, restyled with BMW tokens) components/layout/ app shell, backend health badge components/evidence/ citation block, hit card, filter select features/evidence/ evidence explorer (live, uses the API) features/chat/ chat workspace shell (orchestrator not connected yet) lib/api.ts typed API client types/api.ts mirrors backend/app/api/schemas.py supabase/migrations/ schema, applied in filename order docs/ architecture, decisions, requirements skills/ agent skills (database setup, scripts) data/ provided BMW files, gitignored Makefile .env.example common tasks and the environment template (one .env at the repo root) ``` ## Rules - **Dependencies point inward.** `api` calls `knowledge` and `orchestration`; `agents` call `knowledge`; `knowledge` talks to the database. `api` never writes SQL, and nothing imports from `api`. - **Python imports are `app.`**, scripts run as `python -m app..`, so paths never depend on the working directory. - **One source for response shapes:** `backend/app/api/schemas.py`, mirrored by `frontend/src/types/api.ts`. Change both together. - **Every API result that states a fact carries a citation** (file, location, verbatim quote). - **UI follows `design.md`:** BMW tokens, rectangular components, no shadows, Inter 300/700 as the approved substitute font, no dark theme. Components keep labels above fields and show loading, empty and error states. - **Tests:** `make test` for the backend (the API tests replace the knowledge tools with fakes). The frontend is checked by `make build` (type-check and bundle) and `make lint`; it has no test runner yet. ## API today | Endpoint | Returns | |---|---| | `GET /api/health` | database and OpenAI-key status (never connection details) | | `GET /api/evidence/search?q=&source=feedback\|docs&line=&market=&domain=&polarity=&powertrain=&k=` | cited hits, hybrid vector and keyword search | | `GET /api/evidence/stats?group_by=&line=&market=...` | exact counts and their total | | `GET /api/evidence/filters` | the values the UI offers as filters | | `GET /api/evidence/{kind}/{id}` | the citation for one stored row | Bad parameters give 422, unknown rows 404, and an unreachable database 503 with no internals in the message. Interactive docs are served at `/docs`. ## Not built yet - Chat endpoints and the orchestrator that plans and runs agents (needs the `conversation` and `message` tables and the new step states from decision 0005). - Authentication: the API is open, which is fine for a local demo and must change before it is exposed. - A Docker setup and CI. # attention_is_all_we_have BMW "AI for Product Decision Making" hackathon — a multi-agent system that turns customer feedback, product data, sales data, and web research into cited, PM-approved vehicle requirements. Software idea: [`docs/idea.md`](docs/idea.md). Architecture docs: [`docs/README.md`](docs/README.md). Agent/push rules: [`AGENTS.md`](AGENTS.md). Repo layout: [`docs/architecture/12-repo-structure.md`](docs/architecture/12-repo-structure.md). ## Layout ``` backend/ FastAPI app, agents, knowledge layer, ingestion, orchestration (Python package `app`) frontend/ Vite + React + TypeScript + Tailwind + shadcn/ui (BMW design tokens) supabase/ SQL migrations docs/ architecture, decisions, requirements skills/ agent skills (database setup) data/ provided BMW files (gitignored) ``` ## Frontend The responsive PM workspace lives in [`frontend/`](frontend/README.md). It implements the documented overview, editable successor targets, requirement reviews, guided research gates, evidence library, and programme reports using the BMW design tokens. The current frontend uses clearly labeled illustrative data and browser storage; it does not call the agent backend yet. ```bash cd frontend npm ci npm run dev ``` See the [frontend guide](frontend/README.md) for build, browser tests, and Vercel deployment. Live demo: [bmw-product-intelligence.vercel.app](https://bmw-product-intelligence.vercel.app). ## Setup 1. Put the provided BMW files in `data/` (gitignored) if you want to re-run the loaders. The data is already loaded in Supabase. 2. `cp .env.example .env` and fill in `OPENAI_API_KEY` and `SUPABASE_DB_URL` (see [`skills/database-setup/SKILL.md`](skills/database-setup/SKILL.md)). 3. `make install` (Python 3.11+, Node 20+, pnpm). PDF loaders also need `pdftotext`/`pdfinfo` (poppler). 4. `make check-db` to verify the database connection and the OpenAI key. ## Run ``` make dev # backend on :8000 and frontend on :5173 (BACKEND_PORT=8001 make dev if 8000 is taken) make backend # API only: http://localhost:8000/api/health, interactive docs at /docs make frontend # UI only: http://localhost:5173 (proxies /api to the backend) make test # backend tests, no database or OpenAI key needed make build # type-check and build the frontend ``` The UI has two screens: **Chat** (the research workspace; the orchestrator is not connected yet) and **Evidence** (search the stored feedback and catalog text, with exact counts; every result shows its file, location and verbatim quote). ## Load and query data Run from any directory after `make install` (the scripts find the root `.env` and `data/` themselves): ``` python -m app.ingest.load_pdfs # chunk + embed the catalog PDFs python -m app.ingest.load_excel # feedback, sales, customer studies python -m app.ingest.load_options # equipment options with per-variant availability python -m app.ingest.seed_ontology # domains, vehicle lines, markets, category labels python -m app.knowledge.tools # demo of the agent retrieval tools (search, lookups, counts, cite) python -m app.ingest.ask_pdf "Welche Felgen gibt es für den 5er?" --line G60 ``` Use the repo's virtualenv (`.venv/bin/python`) or activate it first. ## Market & Trend Agent The first agent implementation is the Market & Trend Agent. It turns cited web research into `market_trend` findings, keeps URL + retrieval date locators, stores web source trust tiers, and leaves the step in `awaiting_review` for PM acceptance. ``` python -m app.agents.market_trend_agent "What comfort trends matter for premium sedans?" --vehicle-line G60 --market US --dry-run python -m app.agents.market_trend_agent "What comfort trends matter for premium sedans?" --vehicle-line G60 --market US --run-id ``` For deterministic demos or tests, pass `--seed-sources path/to/sources.json` with a JSON list of `url`, `title`, and `snippet` entries. To avoid OpenAI as well, pass a model-output fixture via `--draft-json`: ``` python -m app.agents.market_trend_agent "comfort trends" --vehicle-line G60 --market US \ --seed-sources backend/tests/fixtures/market_trend_sources.json \ --draft-json backend/tests/fixtures/market_trend_draft.json \ --dry-run ``` # Tech stack > Status: `building` · Last updated: 2026-10-10 (local demo frontend and Vercel, see decision 0011) Kept boring on purpose — a hackathon is not the place to debug infrastructure. | Layer | Choice | Why | |---|---|---| | Orchestration | LangGraph | Its explicit interrupt-for-human-input pattern maps directly onto the per-step PM gates in [`02-orchestration-and-human-in-the-loop.md`](02-orchestration-and-human-in-the-loop.md) — one `interrupt()` per `Step`, not one at the end, plus a planner node where the orchestrator chooses the agents. Its Postgres checkpointer stores run state in the same Supabase database (use the direct or session-pooler connection string, not the transaction pooler) | | LLM | Every agent is LLM-backed. Currently the OpenAI API (key in `.env`); the provider is a config choice and Claude remains an option | Extraction, cluster labeling, requirement drafting, scoring rationale, Critic verification, answering over retrieved evidence. Answers may only cite retrieved rows | | Web research | The LLM's built-in web search tool (OpenAI Responses API `web_search`), for now | No extra search API key or service. Sources are built from the tool's citation annotations, not from model-written text; source-trust tagging is applied at ingest time. A dedicated search API (Tavily/Brave) stays an option, see [decision 0009](../decisions/0009-web-search-through-the-llm.md) | | PDF parsing | `pdftotext -layout` (poppler) for text; pdfplumber / vision-LLM still planned for the equipment tables | Text extraction works (the catalogs have real text). Reliable ■/□ column mapping needs table-aware extraction or a vision pass — not built yet | | Excel | openpyxl (+ psycopg for loading) | Loaders in `backend/app/ingest/`; the customer-study cross-tabs need a custom parser | | Storage | Supabase (managed Postgres) + pgvector 0.8 | One database for both relational entities (`Finding`, `Requirement`, `AuditEvent`, …) and embeddings — keeps traceability joins simple instead of reconciling two stores. Schema is live: see `supabase/migrations/`. RLS is on for every table with no policies yet, so only the backend (service role / direct connection) can read or write; the frontend goes through the API | | Embeddings | OpenAI `text-embedding-3-small` (1536 dims, cosine, HNSW) | Key in `.env` as `OPENAI_API_KEY`. Only `finding.text` and `chunk.content` are embedded; option codes and sales numbers stay exact, un-embedded data. Changing the model means re-embedding and altering the column — see [decision 0004](../decisions/0004-supabase-and-openai-embeddings.md) | | API | FastAPI (`backend/app/api`), served by uvicorn | Evidence endpoints are implemented. Authentication and live orchestration remain future work; see [`12-repo-structure.md`](12-repo-structure.md) | | Frontend | React + TypeScript + Vite; Radix primitives and variant-based components following the shadcn pattern | Implemented in `frontend/`: scoped overview, targets, portfolio, review gates, evidence, reports, and local decision history. BMW tokens, self-hosted Inter, Phosphor icons; see [decision 0011](../decisions/0011-local-demo-frontend-and-vercel.md) | | Frontend persistence | Browser local storage (demo only) | Illustrative fixtures, local edits and previews, JSON/CSV export. No shared or immutable server persistence | | Deploy | Static Vercel frontend; Supabase hosts the backend database | Deploy `frontend/` as Vite. Python services are separate and are not deployed with this frontend. import re

from pathlib import Path

sha = subprocess.check_output(["git", "rev-parse", "HEAD"], text=True).strip()
title = lambda s: (re.search(r"^#\s+(.+)$", s, re.M) or [None, None])[1]
status = lambda s: (re.search(r"Status:\s*`?([a-z]+)`?", s) or [None, None])[1]

decisions = sorted(Path("docs/decisions").glob("0*.md"))
architecture = sorted(Path("docs/architecture").glob("*.md"))
if dry:

conn = psycopg.connect(os.environ["SUPABASE_DB_URL"], autocommit=True)
with conn.transaction():
    for p in decisions:
        s = p.read_text()
        conn.execute(
            "insert into design_decisions (id, title, status, body, source_path, commit_sha, updated_at) "
            "values (%s,%s,%s,%s,%s,%s,now()) on conflict (id) do update set title=excluded.title, "
            "status=excluded.status, body=excluded.body, source_path=excluded.source_path, "
            "commit_sha=excluded.commit_sha, updated_at=now()",

            "status=excluded.status, body=excluded.body, commit_sha=excluded.commit_sha, updated_at=now()",

problems: list[str] = []

if not url:
    bad("SUPABASE_DB_URL is not set in .env (see skills/database-setup/SKILL.md)")

u = urlparse(url)
ok(f"SUPABASE_DB_URL set -> host {u.hostname}, port {u.port}, user {u.username}")
if u.port == 6543:
    bad("port 6543 is the transaction pooler: use the session pooler (5432) or the direct connection")
if "[YOUR-PASSWORD]" in url:
    bad("the connection string still contains the [YOUR-PASSWORD] placeholder")
(ok if os.environ.get("OPENAI_API_KEY") else bad)("OPENAI_API_KEY " + ("set" if os.environ.get("OPENAI_API_KEY") else "missing (needed for embeddings and search)"))
